items.headline: U.S. loses measles-elimination status
items.summary: An international health body determined that endemic outbreaks mean the U.S. is no longer considered measles-free, the first such loss in 26 years. Doctors are also raising alarms about babies born with congenital measles.

items.headline: Ukraine collapses a span of the Kerch Bridge
items.summary: Ukraine said its drones and missiles brought down an arch and a road span of the bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, severing the road link. The Kremlin said the bridge will be restored, and Russia claimed it downed 1,441 drones in one night.

items.headline: U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island
items.summary: The U.S. carried out new strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island. Vice President JD Vance said the Iran conflict will not become a forever war.

items.headline: White House sends Congress $50 billion air traffic plan
items.summary: The administration formally detailed a $50.1 billion request to modernize air traffic control and improve airports after last week's nationwide ground stop. Sen. Jack Reed said the FAA needs a real plan and better contractor oversight, not just more money.

items.headline: Nvidia board rules out Huang's return
items.summary: Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, after Huang said he would be honored to return. Huang has agreed to testify to Congress.

items.headline: Protests greet Trump in Manila
items.summary: Activists, students and Indigenous groups protested as the Philippine government welcomed President Trump, with more than 200 people arrested on Sunday. The protests target a U.S.-backed tech hub that would displace an Aeta community.

items.headline: Van Hollen challenges Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
items.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen's bid to replace Chuck Schumer sets up a Dec. 1 leadership vote. The contest is pressuring Senate Democrats to take sides after their midterm gains.

items.headline: Big U.S. data centers out-emit Denmark
items.summary: A Nature Sustainability study estimates the 400 largest U.S. data centers produced about 28.3 million tons of carbon dioxide in a year, more than Denmark. They used nearly 2% of U.S. energy.

items.headline: China and Canada cut more tariffs
items.summary: Xi Jinping and Mark Carney agreed that China will ease duties on about C$400 million of Canadian exports, including pork and seafood. Canada will extend tariff exemptions on some Chinese steel and aluminum for two years.

items.headline: Apple outage adds to string of tech failures
items.summary: Apple reported full outages of Apple Music, the App Store and AppleCare after an update went wrong. It followed recent breakdowns at banks, airlines and the FAA.

digest.overview:
International health officials said the United States is no longer measles-free, the first loss of that status in 26 years. The administration formally asked Congress for $50.1 billion to overhaul air traffic control, while Sen. Jack Reed said the FAA needs a real plan; flight cancellations have fallen sharply, and about 6 million people are expected to fly for Thanksgiving. Nvidia's chair said the board will not reinstate Jensen Huang, who has agreed to testify to Congress. Apple suffered outages of Apple Music and the App Store, the latest in a string of tech breakdowns. Sen. Chris Van Hollen is challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader in a Dec. 1 vote. A study found the 400 largest U.S. data centers emitted more carbon dioxide in a year than Denmark, and Joe Biden released a memoir about his presidency and his 2024 exit.

Abroad, Ukraine said its drones and missiles collapsed a road span of the Kerch Bridge to Crimea, and the Kremlin vowed to restore it as Russia claimed 1,441 drones downed in one night. The U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island, and a gas tanker burned in the Strait of Hormuz. In Manila, protests greeted President Trump, with more than 200 arrested on Sunday, and he said he could meet Kim Jong Un in China around the APEC summit in Shenzhen. South Korean President Lee Jae-myung and Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi held a summit on the sidelines of the ASEAN meeting in the Philippines. In Shenzhen, Xi Jinping and Mark Carney agreed on new tariff relief for Canadian pork and seafood and Chinese steel and aluminum.

home.overview:
Quentin Grimes erupted for a career-high 47 points and 10 threes as the Lakers rallied past Charlotte 118–114 in overtime for their ninth straight win. Brice Sensabaugh poured in 40 off the bench to end Utah's 12-game skid with a 132–107 rout of the Clippers, Cade Cunningham's 27 sent Detroit past San Antonio 105–93, Jalen Brunson scored 31 in the Knicks' win at Toronto and Minnesota edged Portland 106–105. Twelve NBA games follow tonight, including Boston at Denver. In baseball, Ryan Jeffers and David Bednar accepted qualifying offers while Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki hit the open market, and Week 11 of the NFL opens Thursday with the Colts at Houston.

Mauricio Pochettino signed off with a 2–0 win over Haiti, sealed by Christian Pulisic's overhead kick, sending the USA into the Concacaf Nations League semifinals. Erling Haaland's stoppage-time penalty completed Norway's comeback from 2–0 down in Denmark, Portugal won 3–2 in Wales, and Friday's draw sets the Nations League quarterfinals. South Korea beat Qatar 1–0, and club football returns this weekend with Bayern–Köln on Friday and the Premier League on Saturday. In the KBO, Doosan made the first free-agent signing of the winter, keeping catcher Yang Eui-ji on a two-year deal worth up to 5.5 billion won.

fact.answer:
Ocean salt comes mostly from rocks on land. Rain absorbs carbon dioxide, which makes it slightly acidic, so it slowly erodes rock and frees salts and minerals as ions that rivers carry to the sea. Hydrothermal vents and undersea volcanoes add more from the seafloor.

Marine life uses up many of those ions, but others stay behind and build up over very long periods. Chloride and sodium dominate, making up about 85 percent of all dissolved ions, with magnesium and sulfate adding about 10 percent more.

Seawater averages about 3.5 percent salt by weight, roughly 35 parts per thousand. According to the USGS, spreading all of the ocean's salt over the land would leave a layer more than 500 feet thick.
